name: NYT Connections
ability_definition: The ability to generate or use different sets of rules for combining or grouping things in different ways.

task_realism.reasoning: Workplace uses of category flexibility include reclassifying inventory, restructuring taxonomies, re-sorting cases by different criteria, and regrouping customer segments or data fields. Connections exercises the same mental move of dropping one grouping rule for another. But it does so through recreational wordplay (homophones, fill-in-the-blank, trivia categories) that rarely appears in real work. Its categories are designed to be clever, not useful.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Each puzzle is a self-contained, zero-stakes, text-only prompt with no tools, no domain context, and a fixed, puzzle-setter-intended answer. Real regrouping work is driven by goals and stakeholders. It usually admits several valid partitions judged by usefulness, and it draws on domain knowledge and iteration. The deliberate decoys are artificial adversarial pressure, not the kind of ambiguity that occurs naturally at work.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The benchmark hits the core of the construct well. Items can be grouped under competing rules, and the solver must resist salient but wrong groupings. However, it tests using and recognizing alternative rules more than generating new ones. It is limited to English lexical items, uses a rigid 4x4 structure with exactly one correct partition, and does not score the quality of the rules or their usefulness for a purpose.

format_match.reasoning: The input is 16 isolated words and the output is four equal-sized groups of four. Real work artifacts are messier: spreadsheets of records, document collections, product catalogs, or case files with many attributes. Groups there vary in size, and the output is often a scheme or rationale rather than a single forced partition.

transferability_reasoning: NYT Connections is a faithful probe of the core cognitive act in Category Flexibility: abandoning an obvious grouping rule for a less obvious one under decoy pressure. That gives it moderate construct validity. Its transfer to workplace capability is limited because the tasks are lexical puzzles with a single intended answer, a toy 4x4 format, and no goal-driven context. It also emphasizes applying hidden rules over generating useful new classification schemes.

2024.metric: leaderboard score on a 0-100 scale (mean per-puzzle score on NYT Connections puzzles)
2024.human_reference: General adult English speakers who do word and category puzzles, i.e. typical NYT Connections players rather than expert puzzlers.
